Under the marketing is a working template: signup, US$250 funding, configuration, then automatic or manual trading across 10 assets with the demo running beside the live account.
The scorecard reflects what the platform publishes, not what its ads promise. We checked the claims against the pages, looked for independent verification, and marked the gaps we found.
whatItClaims: A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
AI and algorithmic market analysis producing signals and suggested entries.
Automatic or manual execution, with a browser-based platform.
whatWeChecked: The fine print: clauses that qualify the headline promises.
The fee framing: no platform fees, but spreads embedded in every trade.
The support story: around-the-clock coverage claimed, exact figures conflicting.
The geo-restrictions: two lists on the page that do not agree.
The template marks: unfilled placeholders left in the wording.
The performance story: no verified track record behind the return claims.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Register with your name, email and phone number, and confirm via the email you are sent.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Complete the US$250 deposit to unlock the live dashboard.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your preferences, select automatic or manual execution, and run the practice account first.

pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: One figure doing two different jobs.
redFlags: A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.
The demo promised in the pitch but buried in the flow.

faqs.q: Can I trade manually?
faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: How fast are withdrawals?
faqs.a: The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

bottomLine: The service behind the marketing looks functional, and a careful user can use it without stepping on the fine print.
Our 4.3 reflects what the pages publish and what they skip. It is not a warning off - it is a reminder to trade the product, not the pitch.
